summary: Sick in office: {doctor} tells you, or {household member}, that it is serious, in the middle of your term or your race.
realLife: One life: He had a brain tumor removed in 1993, and in 2005, as the new Judiciary chair, worked through chemotherapy for Hodgkin's lymphoma; a colleague shaved his head in solidarity. Another: The day after the 2004 concession he announced his wife's breast cancer. When it returned in 2007, the couple chose to keep his campaign going. Another: Years after leaving office her cancer returned, and she said publicly she had made peace with it.
gates: You hold an office or are running.
A serious diagnosis is on record for you or someone in your household.
weights: How far into the term or race you are.
How much the work needs you there in person.

branches.then: A colleague shaves his head with you, and your committee keeps meeting.

branches.when: {household member}'s illness comes back during the race
branches.then: You and {household member} decide to keep campaigning together.

branches.when: it comes back after you leave office
branches.then: You say in public that you have made peace, and the place honors you at the end.
